notes: encoding::csv: Go's Reader and Writer ported from Go's line-based readRecord and Write, with Go's quoting, CRLF, comment, TrimLeadingSpace, LazyQuotes, FieldsPerRecord and ParseError messages; differential-checked by tools/encoding_conformance.py (Read event sequences with positions and offsets, and WriteAll output). Deviations forced by Rust: Comma and Comment are chars, and Comment None is Go's zero rune; Read returns Result<Option<Vec<String>>, Error>, with None at end of input; Reader::read_raw is Go's Read: byte fields, with the partial record returned alongside parse, field-count and I/O errors (checked with injected read failures and invalid UTF-8); Reader::read is the Result-shaped String form; TrailingComma has no effect, as in Go; FieldPos panics out of range as Go does; Writer.Flush and WriteAll return io::Result and Writer.Error returns the sticky error as an Option. Limits are Rust-only opt-in input budgets, unlimited by default

ErrTrailingComma.note: Go's reader does not return it; kept for the same source-level surface

ParseError.Err.note: a SentinelError, which Display-prints the same message as Go's sentinel errors

ParseError.Error.note: the Display impl gives Go's record and parse error messages

ParseError.Unwrap.note: returns the sentinel error as the source

Reader.Comma.note: a char rather than a rune; the delimiter rules are Go's

Reader.Comment.note: Option<char>; None is Go's zero rune

Reader.FieldPos.note: panics on an out-of-range index, as Go does

Reader.FieldsPerRecord.note: isize, with Go's zero and negative meanings

Reader.Read.note: returns (Vec<Vec<u8>>, Option<Error>) as Go returns (record, err): fields are bytes and parse, field-count and I/O errors come with the record; Error::Eof is io.EOF. Reader::read is the Result-shaped String form

Reader.ReadAll.note: byte fields as Go; Reader::read_all is the String form

Reader.ReuseRecord.note: Go only permits Read to share the previous record's storage; read_raw_into reuses the caller's record and field allocations, and the reuse_record flag itself has no further effect

Reader.TrailingComma.note: deprecated in Go and unused by it; it has no effect here either

Writer.Comma.note: a char rather than a rune

Writer.Error.note: returns Option<&io::Error>, the sticky error from a failed write or flush

Writer.Flush.note: returns io::Result<()>; Go discards the error and reports it through Error

Writer.Write.note: returns io::Result<()>; an invalid delimiter is InvalidInput
